summary: `desktop.conf` is the DE-agnostic graphical substrate that every graphical image inherits on top of `base.conf` — it contains everything a desktop needs that is *not* a desktop environment. Concretely: a complete font stack (Latin/CJK/emoji/math/symbols via Fedora's `default-fonts-*` metapackages), the full multimedia codec stack (RPM Fusion `ffmpeg` swapped in over `ffmpeg-free`, the four GStreamer plugin tiers, VA-API/VDPAU/Vulkan hardware decode), PipeWire + WirePlumber as the audio/video server, the DE-agnostic half of XDG desktop portals (`xdg-desktop-portal` + the universal `-gtk` fallback backend, `xdg-dbus-proxy`, `xdg-user-dirs`, `xdg-utils`, `xdg-terminal-exec`), Flatpak with a *declaratively* registered Flathub remote, the OCI container tooling (podman/buildah/skopeo/toolbox/distrobox with netavark, crun, container-selinux), printing via CUPS + Avahi + driver packs, scanning via SANE + sane-airscan, NetworkManager with its wifi/bluetooth/wwan submodules, BlueZ, and the freedesktop session plumbing (polkit, udisks2, upower, gvfs, gnome-keyring/libsecret, at-spi2, gsettings-desktop-schemas, Xwayland, plymouth). It is the layer that makes "any DE dropped on top of this image just works" true, so that a GNOME/KDE/Hyprland manifest only has to name its shell, its session manager, its portal backend, and its display manager. Source: this was previously fused with GNOME inside `/mnt/Andromeda/DEV/fedora-custom-images/config/profiles/workstation.conf`; the split below extracts the ~85% of that file that has nothing to do with GNOME, and fixes four package names in it that do not exist on Fedora 44.

packages.name: default-fonts-core-math

packages.name: default-fonts-cjk-sans

packages.name: default-fonts-cjk-serif
packages.why: CJK serif coverage.

packages.name: default-fonts-cjk-mono

packages.name: default-fonts-other-sans
packages.why: Arabic, Hebrew, Devanagari, Thai, Ethiopic etc. — kills tofu for non-Latin non-CJK scripts.

packages.name: default-fonts-other-serif

packages.name: default-fonts-other-mono
packages.why: Monospace coverage for the same script set.

packages.name: google-noto-sans-symbols-2-fonts

packages.name: dejavu-fonts-all

packages.name: abattis-cantarell-fonts

packages.name: jetbrains-mono-fonts

packages.name: cascadia-code-fonts

packages.name: adobe-source-code-pro-fonts

packages.name: fira-code-fonts

unavailable.name: liberation-fonts
unavailable.alternative: Does not exist on F44 (no package, no Provides). Use `liberation-fonts-all`, or the individual `liberation-sans-fonts` / `liberation-serif-fonts` / `liberation-mono-fonts` / `liberation-narrow-fonts`. This name is currently in workstation.conf and WILL fail the build.

unavailable.name: google-noto-cjk-fonts
unavailable.alternative: Does not exist on F44. Use `default-fonts-cjk-sans` / `-serif` / `-mono`, or directly `google-noto-sans-cjk-fonts` / `google-noto-serif-cjk-fonts` / `google-noto-sans-cjk-vf-fonts`. Also currently in workstation.conf and will fail.

unavailable.name: mesa-va-drivers
unavailable.alternative: Removed as a separate package on F44 — the VA-API drivers are now inside `mesa-dri-drivers` (verified: mesa-dri-drivers owns */dri/radeonsi_drv_video.so). Install `mesa-dri-drivers`, then swap to `mesa-va-drivers-freeworld` for the patent-encumbered build.

unavailable.name: mesa-vdpau-drivers
unavailable.alternative: Likewise gone on F44; VDPAU is deprecated. Rely on VA-API (`mesa-dri-drivers` + `mesa-va-drivers-freeworld`) and Vulkan video.

unavailable.name: google-noto-sans-symbols2-fonts
unavailable.alternative: Typo'd name. The real package is `google-noto-sans-symbols-2-fonts` (hyphen before the 2).

unavailable.name: p7zip / p7zip-plugins
unavailable.alternative: Retired on F44. Use `7zip` (upstream 7-Zip), which is what actually exists.

unavailable.name: langpacks-core-font-en
unavailable.alternative: No `langpacks-core-font-*` subpackages exist on F44 — only `langpacks-core-<lang>` and `langpacks-<lang>`. The font role they used to serve is now covered by the `default-fonts-*` metapackages.

unavailable.name: pipewire-pulse
unavailable.alternative: Debian name. On Fedora it is `pipewire-pulseaudio`.

unavailable.name: xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland
unavailable.alternative: Not in Fedora repos. COPR `solopasha/hyprland` (or `lionheartp/Hyprland`). Belongs in a Hyprland DE layer, not here.

unavailable.name: libdvdcss
unavailable.alternative: Not in rpmfusion-free/nonfree — it lives in the separate `rpmfusion-free-tainted` repo, which is not enabled in the base layer. Enable rpmfusion-free-tainted explicitly if encrypted DVD playback is required, or omit.

unavailable.name: epson-inkjet-printer-escpr
unavailable.alternative: Not in Fedora repos. Upstream RPM from download.ebz.epson.net, or COPR. Only add if Epson printers are in scope.

unavailable.name: mtpfs
unavailable.alternative: Not in F44 repos. `gvfs-mtp` + `libmtp` cover MTP access via GIO/gvfs-fuse, which is what desktops actually use.

unavailable.name: gstreamer1-vaapi
unavailable.alternative: Exists on F44 but only in the frozen `fedora` repo, not `updates` — it is deprecated upstream. Do NOT install it; the `va` plugin inside `gstreamer1-plugins-bad-free` is the supported replacement and coexisting can cause double-init crashes.

integration.detail: Flathub remote, declaratively: write `/usr/share/flatpak/remotes.d/flathub.flatpakrepo` (or `/etc/flatpak/remotes.d/`) in the image. Flatpak 1.18 (F44) reads remotes.d at runtime with no D-Bus, no session bus, no network at build time. This replaces the current `RUN flatpak remote-add --system` line, which only appears to work because of the `|| true`.

Flatpak app pre-seeding: drop `.preinstall` files into `/usr/share/flatpak/preinstall.d/` (F44's flatpak ships this directory plus `flatpak-preinstall(1)`). This is the correct declarative mechanism; DE and purpose layers add their own files here, so desktop.conf only has to guarantee the directory and the trigger unit exist.

Ship a first-boot oneshot: `flatpak-preinstall.service` with `Type=oneshot`, `After=network-online.target flatpak-system-helper.service`, `ExecStart=/usr/bin/flatpak preinstall -y --system`, `ConditionPathExists=!/var/lib/flatpak/.preinstall-done`. Fedora does NOT ship such a unit (verified: no package provides flatpak-preinstall.service), so this is ours to write. Enable it via `systemctl enable`.

PipeWire and WirePlumber are USER units. `systemctl enable pipewire` in a Containerfile is wrong/no-op. Use `systemctl --global enable pipewire.socket pipewire-pulse.socket wireplumber.service`, which writes into /etc/systemd/user/ and applies to every user. This is a real, easy-to-miss correctness bug.

SANE ships `/usr/lib/udev/rules.d/60-libsane.rules` which chgrp's scanner devices to the `scanner` group. On a bootc image with no traditional %post, guarantee the group exists via sysusers (below) or scanners are root-only.

Create desktop-relevant groups declaratively with `/usr/lib/sysusers.d/desktop-common.conf`: `g scanner -`, `g plugdev -`, `g lp -`, `g render -`, `g video -`, `g input -`, `g dialout -`. systemd-sysusers runs on every boot and is the only reliable way to guarantee group existence on an image whose /etc is a merged overlay.

Rootless podman needs `/etc/subuid` and `/etc/subgid` entries per user. Set `SUB_UID_MIN`/`SUB_GID_MIN`/`SUB_UID_COUNT` in `/etc/login.defs` and ensure `useradd` allocates ranges (`USE_SUBORDINATE_IDS yes`), so users created after deploy get ranges automatically. Baking /etc/subuid entries for a user that does not exist yet is a common bootc mistake.

`/etc/containers/registries.conf.d/00-unqualified.conf` setting `unqualified-search-registries = ["registry.fedoraproject.org", "quay.io", "docker.io"]` so `podman run alpine` and distrobox work without full URLs. Also `/etc/containers/storage.conf` driver=overlay with `mountopt=nodev,metacopy=on`.
`/etc/xdg/user-dirs.defaults` and `/etc/xdg/user-dirs.conf` to control which XDG dirs get created (e.g. drop Templates/Public) uniformly across all DEs.
`container-selinux` and `flatpak-selinux` must be installed, and the build should NOT relabel /var. Also consider `setsebool -P cups_execmem on` only if a driver needs it — do not blanket-permissive.

Plymouth requires `rhgb quiet` in the kernel cmdline to actually show. On bootc, set this via `/usr/lib/bootc/kargs.d/10-desktop.toml` with `kargs = ["rhgb", "quiet"]` — this is the bootc-native mechanism and survives upgrades, unlike editing grub.
Optionally `/usr/lib/bootc/kargs.d/20-audio.toml` for `snd_hda_intel.dmic_detect=0` on machines where SOF misdetects; leave commented as a documented escape hatch rather than default-on.
`systemctl set-default graphical.target` — belongs here, not in a DE layer, since every graphical image needs it and DE layers only differ in which display manager they enable.

Run `update-desktop-database /usr/share/applications` and `update-mime-database /usr/share/mime` as the last step of the layer's RUN, plus `fc-cache -f` — RPM scriptlets write these caches, but layering order across multiple Containerfile stages can leave them stale, producing 'no application found to open this file' on a fresh deploy.

`/usr/lib/sysctl.d/60-desktop.conf`: `fs.inotify.max_user_watches=524288` (editors/file managers/Syncthing exhaust the default), `fs.inotify.max_user_instances=1024`, `kernel.dmesg_restrict=0` only if you want unprivileged journal diagnostics (otherwise leave hardened).

`/etc/security/limits.d/95-pipewire.conf` with `@audio - rtprio 95` / `- memlock 4194304` is the traditional approach, but with `rtkit` installed it is unnecessary and arguably worse. Prefer rtkit; only add limits.conf if a purpose layer does pro-audio.

Mask `systemd-networkd` / `systemd-resolved` conflicts are already handled by NetworkManager's preset, but explicitly enable `NetworkManager-wait-online.service` ONLY if a purpose layer needs it — it adds boot latency on every laptop and should be off by default in a desktop layer.

`ostree container commit` / `bootc container lint` as the final Containerfile step, and `dnf clean all && rm -rf /var/cache/* /var/lib/dnf` — anything left in /var bloats the image and is then discarded at deploy anyway.

flatpaks: org.gnome.Platform and org.kde.Platform runtimes (pre-seed both so first launch of any app is fast on either DE)
org.freedesktop.Platform.ffmpeg-full (codec extension — makes Flatpak media apps decode everything without the host codec stack)
com.github.tchx84.Flatseal (permission management; the one Flatpak-management tool that is genuinely DE-agnostic)
org.mozilla.firefox (fast-moving, sandboxed, upstream-built — better as Flatpak than as an RPM baked into an immutable image)
com.brave.Browser / com.google.Chrome / com.microsoft.Edge (proprietary browsers: Flatpak avoids adding a third-party RPM repo to the image and the associated GPG-key and upgrade-breakage risk)
com.valvesoftware.Steam (proprietary, huge, self-updating — never bake as RPM)
org.libreoffice.LibreOffice (moves ~1 GB out of the image)
copr: solopasha/hyprland — xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland and friends. Listed only to be explicit that it is NOT needed here; it belongs to the Hyprland DE layer.

(none required for desktop.conf itself — every package above is in fedora/updates/rpmfusion-free/rpmfusion-nonfree, which is a deliberate design goal for this layer: the shared layer must not depend on any COPR, because a COPR going stale would break every image at once.)

external.name: Flathub remote definition (flathub.flatpakrepo)
external.method: Fetch `https://dl.flathub.org/repo/flathub.flatpakrepo` at build time and COPY it into `/usr/share/flatpak/remotes.d/`. Do NOT use `RUN flatpak remote-add`. Alternatively install the `fedora-flathub-remote` RPM, but note it ships only the *filtered* Fedora-approved subset (`/usr/share/flatpak/fedora-flathub.filter`), which excludes many apps — usually not what you want.

external.name: rpmfusion-free-tainted repo
external.method: Only if libdvdcss (encrypted DVD) is required: `dnf install rpmfusion-free-release-tainted` then `dnf install libdvdcss`. Adds legal exposure; recommend leaving out of the shared layer.

external.name: Epson ESC/P-R printer driver
external.method: Upstream RPM from download.ebz.epson.net. Purpose-layer concern, not shared.

risks: ffmpeg vs ffmpeg-free is the #1 build-breaker. Fedora's base pulls `ffmpeg-free`, and `gstreamer1-plugin-libav` links its ABI. Plain `dnf install ffmpeg` will fail on file conflicts. The layer MUST use `dnf swap ffmpeg-free ffmpeg --allowerasing -y` (or `dnf install --allowerasing`) BEFORE installing the gstreamer set, and then reinstall gstreamer1-plugin-libav so it rebinds. Verified both packages exist and both own libav* paths.

mesa-va-drivers-freeworld / mesa-vulkan-drivers-freeworld conflict with the Fedora originals. On F44 the VA drivers were folded into `mesa-dri-drivers`, so the freeworld swap semantics changed — test `dnf swap mesa-va-drivers mesa-va-drivers-freeworld` fails now. Use `dnf install --allowerasing mesa-va-drivers-freeworld` and verify with `vainfo` in a smoke test, because a silent fallback to software decode is invisible until a user complains about battery life.

`RUN flatpak install --system` inside a container build is unreliable and should be removed from the current Containerfile. Two independent failure modes: (1) there is no session/system D-Bus in a buildah/podman build, so flatpak-system-helper cannot be reached — running as root sometimes bypasses this, which is exactly why the failure is intermittent rather than clean; (2) more fundamentally, flatpak installs into /var/lib/flatpak, and bootc treats /var as machine-local mutable state. Image /var is only seeded on *initial install* and is NOT updated on `bootc upgrade`, so baked Flatpaks either vanish or silently freeze at the version from the day the machine was first provisioned. Correct mechanism: declarative remote in /usr/share/flatpak/remotes.d + /usr/share/flatpak/preinstall.d entries + a first-boot systemd oneshot running `flatpak preinstall -y --system`. Everything in /usr, nothing in /var at build time.
Similarly, `flatpak remote-add --system` writes to /var/lib/flatpak/repo/config — same /var problem. The `|| true` in the current Containerfile masks the failure entirely.

Baking RPM Fusion codecs (x264, x265, ffmpeg, gstreamer1-plugins-ugly, libavcodec-freeworld, unrar) into a published image is a redistribution act, not a personal-use act. If the image is pushed to a public registry, patent (H.264/HEVC) and license (unrar is non-free, no redistribution of derived source) exposure attaches to whoever publishes it. Consider splitting a `desktop-codecs.conf` that private builds include and public builds omit.

`system-config-printer` and `xdg-user-dirs-gtk` and `gnome-keyring` are GTK/GNOME-linked. They are behaviorally DE-agnostic (all three work fine under KDE/Hyprland), but a KDE layer will want to swap gnome-keyring for kwallet and system-config-printer for print-manager. Make these three overridable rather than hard-coded, or a KDE image ships two secret services and users get double password prompts.
`hplip` is ~29 MB installed plus a large dependency tail (Python, Qt for hplip-gui). If the fleet has no HP printers this is pure waste; consider gating it.
`pipewire-jack-audio-connection-kit` Provides/Obsoletes jack-audio-connection-kit. Any purpose layer that installs real JACK (audio production) will conflict. Document it.

`libva-intel-media-driver` (Fedora, free) and `intel-media-driver` (RPM Fusion nonfree) both exist and conflict. This manifest picks the Fedora one. If a purpose layer needs the nonfree build for a specific codec, it must swap, not add.
`toolbox` and `distrobox` overlap heavily (~12 MB for toolbox alone). Shipping both is defensible for a shared layer but is a deliberate choice, not an accident.

systemd user-unit enablement: `systemctl enable pipewire` at build time silently succeeds-as-noop or errors depending on dnf5/systemd version. If audio is dead on first deploy, this is why. Must be `systemctl --global enable`.

The `fonts` and `multimedia` dnf groups exist and are tempting, but `dnf group install multimedia` pulls `PackageKit-gstreamer-plugin`, which drags PackageKit into an image where PackageKit cannot function (immutable /usr). Prefer the explicit package list above over @multimedia.

SELinux: adding custom systemd units and udev rules under /usr/lib on a bootc image requires correct labels at build time. If the build container has SELinux disabled, labels may be wrong and units will fail to start on an enforcing host. Run `restorecon -R /usr/lib/systemd /usr/lib/udev` as part of the layer, or build with an SELinux-aware buildah.
size_note: Roughly 2.5-3.5 GB installed on top of fedora-bootc, before any DE. Dominated by: fonts ~700-900 MB (CJK alone is ~350-450 MB via the default-fonts-cjk-* metapackages pulling google-noto-*-cjk-vf-fonts; drop CJK and the layer loses ~400 MB); graphics/mesa ~250 MB (mesa-dri-drivers alone is 52 MB, plus vulkan drivers and the freeworld variants); printing ~350 MB (hplip 29 MB + gutenprint 28 MB + foomatic-db 9 MB + ghostscript + the Python/Qt tail behind hplip-gui and system-config-printer); containers ~250 MB (podman 49 MB, toolbox 12 MB, plus buildah/skopeo/crun/netavark); linux-firmware and the firmware subpackage tail ~400-700 MB depending on how many *-firmware subpackages get pulled — this is the single largest and most variable item and the best candidate for trimming on known-hardware fleets; multimedia/gstreamer ~200 MB; scanning ~50 MB; IMEs ~100 MB. The three cheapest big wins if size matters: drop non-CJK `default-fonts-other-*` and the IME set (~150 MB) for Latin-only fleets, drop `hplip` + `foomatic-db` + `gutenprint` (~70 MB plus tail) for driverless-only printing via ipp-usb/sane-airscan, and replace `linux-firmware` with the specific `*-firmware` subpackages for the actual hardware.
notes: THE SPLIT — what came OUT of workstation.conf into desktop.conf: xdg-user-dirs, xdg-utils, xorg-x11-server-Xwayland, all fonts, all ffmpeg/gstreamer, pipewire/pipewire-pulseaudio/wireplumber, podman/buildah/skopeo/toolbox/distrobox, flatpak, cups/system-config-printer, sane-backends, GRAPHICAL_TARGET=true, and the Flathub remote registration. That is 26 of the 30 lines in the current rhel package list.

DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED — belongs to a DE layer, not here: @gnome-desktop (or @kde-desktop/@cosmic-desktop), gdm/sddm/lightdm and any display manager, gnome-tweaks, gnome-extensions-app, gnome-shell/plasma-desktop, gnome-software / plasma-discover (app-store frontends are DE-specific and gnome-software drags PackageKit), the DE's portal backend (xdg-desktop-portal-gnome / -kde / -cosmic / -lxqt / -hyprland — desktop.conf ships only the frontend plus the -gtk fallback), the DE's file manager, terminal, text editor and archive tool, DE-specific theming (gnome-themes-extra, breeze), blueman (GTK tray — GNOME and KDE both have native BT UIs), simple-scan / skanlite (GTK vs Qt scanner frontends — the DE layer picks one; desktop.conf ships only the SANE backends they both drive), gnome-disk-utility, kwallet vs gnome-keyring choice, and `systemctl enable gdm` (the DE layer enables its own DM; desktop.conf only sets graphical.target).

DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED — belongs to a purpose layer: development toolchains, LibreOffice, browsers, Steam/gaming (gamemode, mangohud, the vm.max_map_count bump), medical/DICOM tooling, VPN clients beyond the NetworkManager plugin, NVIDIA drivers (that is a hardware layer — akmod-nvidia has its own kargs, secureboot signing, and RPM Fusion nonfree-nvidia-driver repo concerns that must not be forced on every graphical image).

DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED — already in base.conf, not duplicated except where the desktop adds submodules: NetworkManager (core), firewalld, fwupd, openssh-server, audit, bootc, the CLI utility set. NetworkManager and fwupd appear above only because the desktop needs *additional* subpackages (-wifi, -bluetooth, -wwan) that a server profile must not get.

The current workstation.conf carries a PKGS_debian list. If the refactor keeps multi-distro support, desktop.conf needs a parallel PKGS_debian — but note the Fedora-specific wins here (default-fonts-* metapackages, RPM Fusion, /usr/share/flatpak/preinstall.d) have no clean Debian equivalent, and the ffmpeg swap dance is Fedora-only. Consider whether the Debian path is still worth maintaining, or whether desktop.conf should be declared Fedora-only and the Debian images stay on the old combined profile.

OPEN QUESTION: should `desktop.conf` also own `/usr/lib/bootc/kargs.d/`? Plymouth needs `rhgb quiet` and that is genuinely shared, but kargs.d files from multiple layers merge by filename, so the layers need a numbering convention (10- shared desktop, 20- hardware, 30- purpose) agreed up front or they will silently clobber each other.

OPEN QUESTION: `container-management` and `printing` and `fonts` all exist as real dnf groups (verified). Using @printing would pull samba-client and colord automatically and stay current with Fedora's decisions. The tradeoff is reproducibility — group membership changes between releases without warning. Recommend explicit packages for this shared layer (as above) precisely because it is the one layer where an unexpected change breaks every image.

Recommend a build-time smoke test baked as a script (not a service): verify `fc-list | grep -c CJK`, `vainfo` exits 0, `gst-inspect-1.0 avdec_h264` resolves, `flatpak remotes` lists flathub, `pactl info` after boot. On an immutable image, a codec regression is invisible until deployed.
